extracted.intended_audience: general readers, Stephen King readers, and aspiring writers interested in writing craft
extracted.subtask_description: Summary and overview of Stephen King's On Writing: A Memoir of the Craft, describing the book's sections and the principal pieces of advice King offers to aspiring writers. Useful as a quick reference to the topics King covers (toolbox, craft advice, memoir) rather than the full text of his rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toolbox — English mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Toolbox' section discusses English mechanics and the importance of vocabulary, grammar and style in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents the mechanical foundations writers should master (vocabulary, grammar, style). The Wikipedia summary does not reproduce King's detailed rules, but indicates the Toolbox is where practical, technical aspects of writing are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Writing Is — take writing seriously / writing as telepathy
rubrics_metrics.description: In 'What Writing Is', King compares writing to telepathy and urges the reader to take writing and his advice seriously; he also includes an example of literary description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames writing as a communicative act (telepathy) and stresses seriousness of craft; includes example passages to demonstrate principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: C.V. — use of personal history to illuminate craft
rubrics_metrics.description: 'C.V.' highlights events in King's life that influenced his writing, discussing childhood exposure to writing, early attempts to be published, relationships, and struggles (e.g., substance abuse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses autobiographical material to show how life experience shapes a writer's development; implies that personal history and formative events are a legitimate way to teach and exemplify craft lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: On Writing — practical advice to aspiring writers
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'On Writing' section 'details King's advice to aspiring writers' about the art of writing (general practical and stylistic guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts as the core craft-advice section; Wikipedia does not list King's specific axioms here, but characterizes it as the place for his direct recommendations to writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: On Living: A Postscript — resilience and return-to-writing
rubrics_metrics.description: 'On Living: A Postscript' discusses King's 1999 accident and how it affected his life and return to writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers an example of how life events (trauma, recovery) intersect with the writing life and can be instructive about persistence, adaptation, and continuing to work despite reduced output or physical challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue and plot — emphasized as solid parts of King's advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers (e.g., Julie Woo, Associated Press) praised King's advice as 'solid', specifically noting his advice about dialogue and plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals that King's guidance places emphasis on crafting believable dialogue and coherent plotting as important elements of fiction writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in work habits and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers observed that King 'describes his work habits and environment urging that consistency in those areas can be conducive to good writing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implying a criterion for productive writing practice: regular, consistent writing habits and a supportive environment are recommended for producing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended reading / updated reading list
rubrics_metrics.description: The 10th Anniversary Edition contains an updated reading list from King (the book includes King's reading recommendations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggests that reading widely / following a curated reading list is part of King's pedagogical approach to improving as a writer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived limits of generic advice (pedestrian advice as anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some critics (e.g., John Mark Eberhart) called King's writing recommendations 'so pedestrian' that they were unmemorable, indicating that generic or overfamiliar craft advice can be of limited use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as an implicit warning: craft advice that is overly generic or repeats common axioms may be less helpful; distinctive, concrete examples and personal specificity are more valued.
